class.name: NetwEntityRecord
class.brief_description: One entity's record plane: what it is, who steers it, and where it is in its life.
class.description: The three facts were already separate, which let a caller hold a control state for one entity beside a stage for another and never be told. This puts one handle over all three, so a record answers about one entity or it is not a record. It holds no session and no [Node], which is what lets a record be constructed, configured and read before either exists. That is also why the handle is minted here rather than granted: an entity has an identity before anything is around to number it. The handle comes from [NetwEntityIds] at construction and is released when the record is freed. The facets an entity publishes are held here too, one of each, minted on first ask through [method set_part_factory] and answered unchanged forever after. The record decides that an entity has exactly one scene facet, one interest handle, one prediction handle, one display handle and one component map; the tier that owns those types decides what one is made of. See [enum Part]. [codeblock] var record := NetwEntityRecord.new() # a handle, a control, stage UNBOUND record.entity_id = &"crate" record.advance(2) # ARMED, if the table admits it record.get_control().set_controller(7) [/codeblock] [NetwEntity] holds one of these and reads its own members through it. Reach for this class directly only when writing the entity plane itself.

method.name: adopt_handle
method.description: Takes the handle a standing record already carries and lets go of the one this record was born with, answering [code]false[/code] for a handle [NetwEntityIds] never issued. The release is the point: a birth handle nobody else has seen would otherwise outlive every holder, and the mint never reissues it, so it would be leaked rather than merely idle. Adopting the handle this record already holds is a no-op rather than a release followed by a retain.

method.name: advance
method.description: Moves the record to [param stage], answering [code]false[/code] and changing nothing when the stage table does not admit the edge, so a caller decides for itself whether a refusal is a bug or a duplicate it can drop. The one stage mutator. Legality is [NetwEntityStage]'s table and this class has no second opinion about it: a stage is never re-entered, the terminal stage is terminal, and a reparent is not an edge at all because a record keeps its stage across a move.

method.name: finish_teardown
method.description: Ends a teardown already in flight, announcing [code]despawned[/code] on [param wrapper]. Answers [code]false[/code] for a record no teardown opened, which is what tells a reparent leaving the tree from a despawn leaving it. Legality is the stage table's alone and it refuses in silence, because a live owner leaving the tree is a reparent rather than a mistake.

method.name: hydrate_identity
method.description: Fills an unset [member entity_id] or [member peer_id] from [param owner]'s node name, which is the channel a manual bind flow carries identity on. A caller that already bound either keeps it, and a name that spells no identity fills nothing rather than taking the node's own name for an entity id.

method.name: get_control
method.description: Returns this record's own control state, never shared with another record. Two records answering one control would answer for one entity while claiming to be two.

method.name: get_handle
method.description: Returns the handle naming this entity. Valid from construction, and the same value for the whole life of the record unless [method adopt_handle] replaces it.

method.name: get_stage
method.description: Returns where the record is in its life, as a [NetwEntityStage] value. A fresh record is unbound.

method.name: has_part_factory
method.description: Returns whether anything has registered how to build [param part], so a caller can tell "this build publishes no such facet" from "this record has not been asked for one yet".

method.name: part
method.description: Returns this record's own [param part], building it through the registered factory on the first ask and answering the same object every ask after. [param wrapper] is handed to the factory, which is what a facet binds itself to. Answers [code]null[/code] when no factory is registered for [param part], rather than a fresh object nobody else will ever see: a facet two callers do not share is not a facet.

method.name: admit_control_request
method.description: Arbitrates one control request, answering the peer that may take control or [code]0[/code] for a request nobody grants. An entity whose transfer is fixed refuses without ever asking, so gameplay code is not consulted about a transfer that could not happen. Otherwise the request is announced as [code]control_requested[/code] on [param wrapper] and any listener may refuse it through [method NetwControlRequest.deny]. The refusal is a latch, so the strictest listener wins and connection order decides nothing.

method.name: apply_control
method.description: Applies the settled controller to [param owner]'s multiplayer authority and announces the move on [param wrapper] as [code]control_changed[/code]. A write that moves nothing announces nothing. The record calls the server [code]0[/code] and the engine calls it [code]1[/code], so the two spellings meet here and nowhere else. Whether the write recurses onto children is [method control_recurses].

method.name: begin_despawn
method.description: Opens the teardown window on [param wrapper]: the legality check, the in-flight options, the stage move to despawning, the [code]despawning[/code] announcement, and the clear. Answers [code]false[/code] having changed nothing when the stage table does not admit a teardown, so a template and a record already tearing down are refused rather than announced twice. [member active_despawn_opts] is readable for exactly the length of the announcement, which is what lets a listener branch on the despawn mode. A caller that wants the linger stage moves there itself, after whatever it owes between the two.

method.name: classify_activation
method.description: Decides what an unbound record on a node the tree now holds IS, and answers whether the caller should carry on down the go-live path. A record already past unbound is already classified. A bound identity goes live. An unbound record with no identity is an editor-placed factory scene when [method declares_template] says so, and it declares itself a template and deactivates; every other unbound node stays inert, a bare programmatic node forever and a spawner-produced one until its arm stamps identity.

method.name: deactivate
method.description: Stops [param owner] processing, showing and replicating: the one act a template, a linger and a deactivated spawn all perform. Its synchronizers are left speaking to the server alone, so the server keeps a template visible to itself and clients remove it. Hiding is a property write rather than a type test, because it is meaningful for a visual owner and a bare logic node has no such property to write.

method.name: control_recurses
method.description: Whether an authority write may recurse onto child synchronizers. The one row that is false is the one that trips an engine assertion: in the tree, not ready yet, and not the authoring peer, where the children's network ids are not registered. Public because it is a table a caller can ask rather than a crash it has to avoid. Applied on the orphan at arm, an authority write is therefore recursive on every peer, which is what makes [method Node.is_multiplayer_authority] correct in every child's [method Node._enter_tree] and [method Node._ready] with no role branch inside the components.

method.name: declares_template
method.description: Whether [param owner] is an editor-placed factory scene. Ownership by an enclosing scene is the editor-placement fact; [method template_meta] is the same declaration for scenes assembled without stamping ownership onto the child.

method.name: mark_template
method.description: Declares this record a template, an editor-placed factory scene that stays deactivated and never spawns, deactivating [param owner] when the tree already holds it. Idempotent, because every peer marks its own copy of the same editor scene and a second mark is a duplicate rather than a bug.

method.name: template_meta
method.description: The metadata that marks an assembly-placed spawn-point template whose identity is intentionally unbound.

method.name: transition
method.description: Moves the record to [param stage] and reports out loud when the table refuses, naming [param owner], in every build. The reporting twin of [method advance], which refuses silently so a caller can decide for itself. A refusal that only reported in a debug build would be one a shipping build takes silently, which is the whole reason this twin exists.

method.name: scene_isolation_of
method.description: Whether this scene hosts its own world, answering an instance's own write first and [param owner]'s script declaration second, and the unisolated default when neither declared one.

method.name: scene_label_of
method.description: The non-unique stem naming this scene's archetype, answering an instance's own write first and [param owner]'s script declaration second. Identity is the handle, never this string: two live instances of one arena share a stem and own separate admission boundaries. Read on an orphan, so the script's declaration comes through [method set_scene_declaration_reader] rather than through a session.

method.name: set_scene_declaration_reader
method.description: Registers how a script's scene declaration is read. [param reader] takes the owner node and answers a [Dictionary] carrying [code]label[/code] and [code]isolation[/code], or an empty one when the script declared no scene. Process-wide, because an entity is configured and read before any session exists. The extension drops it at shutdown.

method.name: set_controller
method.description: Records [param peer] as the controller and announces the move as [code]control_changed[/code] on [param wrapper], answering whether anything moved. Writing the value it already holds announces nothing. This records who steers; [method apply_control] is what makes the engine agree.

method.name: set_part_factory
method.description: Registers how to build [param part]. [param factory] takes the wrapper and answers the facet, and it is called at most once per record. Process-wide and outliving every record, because an entity is configured and read before any session exists, exactly as [NetwEntityIds] is. The extension drops every factory at shutdown.

members.member: Whether this entity IS a scene rather than living in one. The ancestor walk that resolves an entity's scene stops at the nearest record answering true, so the answer belongs on the record rather than on the wrapper that walk would otherwise have to ask.
The durable name, the only one of an entity's names that survives the process. Save files, display labels and logs key on it.
The peer this entity represents, or [code]0[/code] when it is server-owned. A non-zero value is the definition of a player entity.

The teardown in flight, or [code]null[/code] outside one. Set for the duration of the [code]despawning[/code] announcement alone, so a listener reads the despawn mode at the one instant it is true. See [method begin_despawn].

The move in flight, or [code]null[/code] outside one. Set before the reparent and cleared after it, so an [code]_exit_tree[/code] consumer can tell a reparent from a despawn and a route survives a move that leaves the tree. See [method NetwMultiplayerCore.entity_move].
The wire name this entity is addressed by, or [code]0[/code] while it is unroutable. Session-monotonic and never reused. See [LivenessShell] for the bridge that assigns it.

constants.constant: The scene facet, which is this entity's own admission boundary when it declares one.
The entity's interest membership and transition configuration.
The entity's prediction and reconciliation configuration.
The entity's display and smoothing settings.
The entity's component-ID map, which addresses a sub-node without a [NodePath].
How many facets a record carries. Not a facet, and asking for it is refused.
